findings.message: `/devcontainer up` and `/devcontainer build` never carry the selected `--config`, so AC-2 is only half met. `handlers["up"]` (src/commands.ts) calls `services.execution.up({ operation: "up", initiator: "slash-command", workspace })` and `handlers["build"]` does the same, while `configPath` reaches the adapter only (a) for `exec`, via the frozen bound selection, or (b) when a caller hand-builds an `UpBuildRequest` with it — which no command-layer caller does. Consequence: in a workspace whose only configuration is a named `.devcontainer/<name>/devcontainer.json` or the legacy root `devcontainer.json`, `/devcontainer up` sends the CLI nothing it can resolve and the start fails, which is the very defect this change set out to fix. My own unit test (container-config-routing.test.ts, "passes an explicit configPath through up and build") drives the SERVICE with a literal request, so it pinned the seam rather than the wiring. Fix: resolve the configuration for the requested workspace in the `up`/`build` handlers (registry entry → selected candidate, or the entry's default candidate) and pass `configPath`, then assert it by invoking the command handler.
